correctness.rationale: Both invertible factors have the same BB* = diag(4,t²). Functional calculus gives 0 ≤ H(I−H) ≤ I/4 and H(I−H) ≤ H on the full complex Hermitian state interval. The first inequality proves forward invariance for both factors. The diagonal factor restricts to logistic 4, which is conjugate to the full tent map via x ↦ sin²(πx/2); the same change of variable pushes the tent map's invariant Lebesgue law to the arcsine law. This proves the entropy lower bound and invariant probability, not chaos on all states. For the swapped factor, congruence preserves order and B² = 2tI, giving Φ²(H) ≤ 4t²H without any monotonicity assumption on Φ. Induction gives the claimed even and odd bounds and uniform convergence; invariance against continuous tests forces δ₀, and separated orbit segments are uniformly bounded in number at each positive scale because all sufficiently late images are close to zero. The proof covers real t in (0,1/2) and all complex Hermitian states. The supplementary checker samples real rational matrices only; it was inspected, not executed, and is not needed for the proof.

value.rationale: The family is a structurally motivated witness that even exact full-rank coupling data, not merely its spectrum, do not determine the qualitative dynamics. It rules out an explanation based on singular factors alone and separates an invariant chaotic subsystem from quantitative extinction for every initial state, including off-diagonal complex Hermitian states. The result needs neither a full-space chaos claim nor a classification of every factorization to make this distinction useful.
